subject: Custody & forwarding controls for LLM outputs
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@meditrust.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Nguyen <victor.nguyen@meditrust.com>, procurement@meditrust.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Custody & forwarding controls for LLM outputs

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this call last week. To move the DPA forward we need clear contractual and operational commitments on three items before our legal & procurement teams will sign:

1) No-model-improvement commitment for customer-generated prompts/responses in production (no training, fine-tuning, or derivative model updates).
2) Explicit ownership/custody language that confirms Meditrust retains rights to prompts and generated responses; Redwood will not assert derivative IP.
3) Controls on cross-border forwarding and subprocessors: list of subprocessors, and an operational plan to route Meditrust traffic to onshore (US) processing and onshore KMS for keys.

Attached is our annotated DPA (MediTrust_DPA_annotated.pdf) — redlines are minimal but these three items are mandatory. We also need evidence (SOC2 report excerpt, subprocessor attestations) by Dec 6 to satisfy our audit window.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) agree contractually to the no-training clause scoped to our tenant, (b) provide a maintained subprocessor inventory and SOC2 evidence, and (c) route our prod workload to US-only instances / onshore KMS?

If possible please also include a proposed DocuSign link and estimated timeline for operational changes.

Thanks,
Alice Park
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
MediTrust Health

Attachments: MediTrust_DPA_annotated.pdf

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@meditrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody & forwarding controls for LLM outputs

Alice —

Appreciate the clear asks. High-level: we can offer a scoped operational + contractual package for Meditrust that addresses all three bullets, but need quick alignment internally on exact wording and delivery dates.

Proposed next steps (short):
- Legal: Marissa, can we draft a one-page addendum that: (i) commits to tenant-scoped non-use for model improvement; (ii) states Meditrust retains ownership of prompts and responses; and (iii) lists export restrictions and audit rights.
- Infra: David, confirm feasibility and ETA for routing Meditrust production traffic to US-only clusters and using onshore KMS for key material.
- I will assemble the subprocessor inventory snapshot and pull SOC2 attestation excerpts for Alice by Dec 6.

I attached our initial redline (Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.pdf) — it contains suggested language that maps to Alice's asks, including a scoped no-training clause and a data egress/export paragraph.

Marissa / David — please reply-all with comment + timeline so I can confirm with Meditrust.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Privacy, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody & forwarding controls for LLM outputs

Hannah / David —

Drafting notes for the addendum:
- No-training clause (tenant-scoped): "Redwood shall not use, access, or incorporate Customer Content (including prompts and generated outputs) for the purposes of improving or training any models, whether proprietary or third-party, without Customer's prior written consent."
- Ownership: explicit sentence that Customer retains all rights in Customer Content and generated outputs; Redwood retains right to monitor for abuse but not assert derivative IP.
- Subprocessors & routing: contract shall require Redwood to maintain an up-to-date subprocessor inventory and provide 30-days' notice of changes; for Meditrust we will commit to routing production requests to US-only processing zones (subject to technical feasibility described by Infra).
- Audit & evidence: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II report excerpt & subprocessor attestations; operational evidence (onshore KMS config, network zoning) provided within the agreed timeline.

Open items for legal ops: acceptable definitions for "Customer Content" and "Model Improvement" (I propose short definitional clauses). We should also limit the no-training commitment to the customer's production tenant(s) and exclude aggregated telemetry necessary for platform health unless it contains Customer Content.

I will prepare the addendum draft by EOD tomorrow.

—Marissa
VP, Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody & forwarding controls for LLM outputs

Hi team — quick operational feasibility:

1) US-only processing: doable. We can pin a customer's production workload to US clusters (us-east-1 primary; fallback in us-west-2) and apply strict routing at the edge. Timeline: ~3 business days to create routing policy + 2 weeks to validate in staging.
2) Onshore KMS: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (customer-owned key) or Redwood-managed keys provisioned in US zones. To guarantee onshore key residency for Meditrust we'll need: (a) KMS key ARN or a request to create a Redwood-managed, US-only CMK; (b) a short runbook to avoid accidental replication across regions. ETA: 2 weeks to configure and test.
3) Subprocessor inventory: attached initial snapshot (subprocessor_inventory_20271129.xlsx). Current subprocessors that touch production customer interactions: AWS (us-east-1), GCP (for non-US analytic workloads), FastCache Inc. (caching), Logstream Ltd. (observability), and DocuSign (signing). For Meditrust we will gate GCP and analytics; only US-region infra will be used for their prod traffic.

Operational caveats: full hard guarantee requires a combination of contractual commitments + a short onboarding checklist (routing policy, KMS binding, and periodic attestation). I estimate we can provide SOC2 excerpts and subprocessor attestations within 4 business days.

David
Sr. Engineering Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Park <alice.park@meditrust.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Victor Nguyen <victor.nguyen@meditrust.com>, procurement@meditrust.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 11:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Custody & forwarding controls for LLM outputs

Hannah —

Thanks, this is encouraging. Please proceed with the addendum Marissa described and the routing/KMS steps David listed. A few final asks:
- Please remove GCP from any processing path for Meditrust production (we want US-only compute and storage).
- Provide the SOC2 excerpt, subprocessor attestations, and the subprocessor_inventory_20271129.xlsx by EOD Dec 6.
- Share DocuSign link and our PO instructions so procurement can close quickly (deal id MT-2027-125).

If we get these items by Dec 6, procurement will push the contract through for signature.

Best,
Alice
Sr. Counsel, Data & Privacy
MediTrust Health
